tool.name: Generate Spin-up Climate Metadata
tool.description: Compute spin-up period dates for SOC model initialization from site metadata

param.name: input_metadata
param.label: Site metadata file
param.help: CSV file describing the experimental sites. Must contain at least the two date columns (see 'First measurement date column' and 'Last measurement date column' below). Other columns (e.g. site_name, longitude, latitude) are preserved but not required by the spin-up computation.

param.name: begin_date_col
param.label: First measurement date column
param.help: Name of the column holding the date of the FIRST SOC measurement (year YYYY or date YYYYMMDD). Default: start_date.

validator.message: The first measurement date column name cannot be empty.

param.name: end_date_col
param.label: Last measurement date column
param.help: Name of the column holding the date of the LAST SOC measurement (year YYYY or date YYYYMMDD). Default: end_date.

validator.message: The last measurement date column name cannot be empty.

param.name: api_source
param.label: Target climate data source
param.help: Indicates which reanalysis dataset will later be used to retrieve climate data. This controls the earliest available date used when clipping the spin-up start: 1959-01-01 for GEOSAS/SAFRAN or 1940-01-01 for Open-Meteo/ERA5 (global).
param.option: Open-Meteo API — ERA5 / ERA5-Land reanalysis (Global, from 1940)

param.name: spinup_min_years
param.label: Minimum spin-up duration (years)
param.help: Minimum number of years required before the first SOC measurement to define a pre-experiment spin-up period. Sites below this threshold will have their spin-up shifted to overlap the first N years of the experiment instead.

param.name: spinup_target_years
param.label: Target spin-up duration (years)
param.help: Ideal length of the spin-up period in years. The effective duration may be shorter if the reanalysis dataset does not extend far enough back in time.

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What this tool does**
This tool computes **spin-up period metadata** for long-term soil organic carbon (SOC) model simulations. It reads a table of experimental site descriptions and, for each site, determines the optimal dates for the model initialization (spin-up) phase — that is, the period of climate data to use to bring the carbon pools to a steady state before the forward simulation begins.
The output is a metadata table listing the spin-up start and end dates, the effective duration, and a plain-language description of the strategy applied. This table can then be passed to a dedicated climate data extraction tool (GEOSAS/SAFRAN or Open-Meteo/ERA5).
The **Target climate data source** parameter controls which reanalysis will be used downstream and therefore sets the earliest date from which data can be requested:
* **GEOSAS / SAFRAN** — French meteorological reanalysis (Météo-France / INRAE GEOSAS). Available from **1959-01-01**. * **Open-Meteo / ERA5** — Global ERA5 and ERA5-Land reanalysis. Available worldwide from **1940-01-01**.
-----
**Input: Site metadata CSV**
Comma-separated file. The tool only reads the two date columns; their names are configurable through the **First measurement date column** and **Last measurement date column** parameters (defaults: ``begin_date`` and ``end_date``). Any other columns are passed through untouched.
+--------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+ | Column (configurable name) | Description | +================================+=============================================================+ | ``begin_date`` *(default)* | Year (YYYY) or date (YYYYMMDD) of the first SOC measurement | +--------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+ | ``end_date`` *(default)* | Year (YYYY) or date (YYYYMMDD) of the last SOC measurement | +--------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+
If a column name given in the parameters is not found in the input file, the tool stops with an explicit error listing the missing column(s).
-----
**Spin-up period logic**
For each site:
1. **Target start** = first measurement date − ``spinup_target_years`` 2. Clip to the **earliest date** available in the chosen reanalysis (``1959-01-01`` for SAFRAN, ``1940-01-01`` for ERA5). 3. **Effective spin-up duration** (years) = first measurement date − clipped start. 4. If effective duration ≥ ``spinup_min_years``:
* Spin-up = [clipped start → first measurement date] *(pre-experiment period)*
5. If effective duration < ``spinup_min_years``:
* Spin-up = [clipped start → clipped start + ``spinup_target_years``] *(first N years of the experiment used instead)*
-----
**Output — Spin-up metadata CSV**
One row per site:
+---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | Column | Description | +===========================+==========================================================+ | ``site_name`` | Site identifier | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``begin_date`` | Date of the first SOC measurement | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``end_date`` | Date of the last SOC measurement | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``start_spinup`` | First day of the spin-up period | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``end_spinup`` | Last day of the spin-up period | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``spinup_duration_yr`` | Effective spin-up duration (years) | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``method_spinup`` | Description of the spin-up strategy applied | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``api_source`` | Target reanalysis (``geosas`` or ``openmeteo``) | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+
Note: in the output, the two date columns are written back using the canonical names ``begin_date`` and ``end_date`` regardless of the input column names.
-----
**References**
* Durand, Y. et al. (1993). A meteorological estimation of relevant parameters for snow models. *Annals of Glaciology*, 18, 65–71. https://doi.org/10.3189/S0260305500011277 * Hersbach, H. et al. (2020). The ERA5 global reanalysis. *Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society*, 146(730), 1999–2049. https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.3803 * Open-Meteo API documentation: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/era5-api * GEOSAS API documentation: https://geosas.fr/web/?page_id=6345
